Funded Research Projects International Association of Schools of Social Work (IASSW) & European Association of Schools of Social Work (EASSW) The International Association of Schools of Social Work (IASSW) and the European Association of Schools of Social Work (EASSW) are pleased to announce a Call for Research Proposals for two collaborative, jointly funded research projects for the funding cycle 2025-2026 that advance the field of social work education, practice, and policy. This initiative aims to foster international collaboration, promote innovative research, and strengthen the global impact of social work scholarship. Objectives We invite proposals that align with the shared mission of IASSW and EASSW to: Advance social work education and research across diverse cultural and regional contexts Promote equity, inclusion, and social justice through academic and practice inquiry Address pressing global challenges such as migration, climate change, peacebuilding, social justice, human rights, diversity and inclusivity, sustainability and digital transformation Strengthen the evidence base for social work education, policy and practice Eligibility Criteria Expressions of interest are welcomed from: Academic institutions affiliated with IASSW and/or EASSW Collaborative teams involving researchers from at least three different countries Projects that demonstrate a clear commitment to interdisciplinary and cross-cultural perspectives Projects must run for up to 24 months. Funding & Support Selected projects will receive joint funding from IASSW (3500$) and EASSW (6000$) . Funding may cover: Research-related expenses (e.g., data collection, analysis) Dissemination activities (e.g., publications, conferences) Collaborative meetings and workshops Details of funding amounts must be provided upon expression of interest. Timeline Deadline for Proposal Submission: 20 November 2025 Notification of Shortlisting: 1 December 2025 Project Start Date: February 2026 Submission Guidelines Interested applicants should submit a proposal (5 A4 pages) including: Project title and summary Research objectives and relevance to EASSW/IASSW priorities Proposed methodology and expected outcomes Composition of the research team and institutional affiliations Budget Please submit your proposal to: smallprojects@eassw.org When submitting your proposal, please use the subject line: Joint EASSW/IASSW Research Project If you want to discuss your proposal before submitting, contact at This is a unique opportunity to contribute to transformative research that bridges continents and communities. We look forward to receiving your innovative and impactful proposals. For inquiries, please contact Assoc. Prof. Panagiotis Pentaris: Panagiotis.Pentaris@gold.ac.uk Visit www.eassw.org and [IASSW Website] for more information.
